tymawr.name: Tŷ Mawr / Great House
tymawr.summary: Tŷ Mawr (“Great House”): the former manorial house at Llandough near Penarth, demolished in December 1988. First named in the 1824 David Stewart survey of the Bute estates as “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; the wider estate is known as Cedwyn.

variants.one_liner: Welsh for “Great House”: the name Cedwyn uses for the former manorial house at Llandough.
Spelling in the 1824 David Stewart survey (plan 19: “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”); alias of Tŷ Mawr / Great House.
Same 1824 survey entry, and HM Land Registry’s wording in its letter of 23 Mar 2026.
Bute estate catalogue wording (“Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm”), undated; also in the place name Cwm Cydfin Wood.
The name this site uses for the wider historic estate around Tŷ Mawr; the record spellings are Cedfin (1824) and Cydfin.
Trade-directory wording, 1868–1901: “Williams John, Great house”.
Slater’s directory spelling, 1880.
Name in the 1881 census (RG11/5288, schedule 9).
Ordnance Survey 25-inch map spelling, north-west of the church.
The English farm name, in Glamorgan Archives D/D XJF 64/30 and in the Historic Environment Record (GGAT02038s).
Newspaper spelling without the circumflex: “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough” (Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958).
Both names side by side, Daily Telegraph, 16 Apr 1974.
English translation of Tŷ Mawr, printed beside it in the Daily Telegraph, 16 Apr 1974.
